# Block 6: Build your own agent in R {.unnumbered} In this block you build the two parts of an agent yourself: a conversation and a tool. Then you run a complete agent on a real task and approve every step it takes. After this, every control from Blocks 3 to 5 is something you can see in code. *⏱ ~35 minutes · Start on `main`, Git pane clean, with your API key saved as `AGENT_ANTHROPIC_KEY` ([setup](11a-setup-claude-code.qmd#api-key)). Claude Code is not used in this block.* :::{.callout-note collapse="true"} ## This block's files, and how it fits You stay in your workshop repository, on `main`, straight after lunch. Claude Code is set aside: you use an agent that you can read line by line. You give it the translation task that the shipped `tests/test_translation.R` checks. Nothing later in the day uses its output. So if time is short, your instructor may run Task 2 on screen while you decide each approval in the chat. | File | Where it comes from | Its job here | |---|---|---| | `data/raw/voles_metabolism.csv` | Shipped; used since Block 2 | The data the translation summarises | | `scripts/functions/load_voles.R` | Shipped; used since Block 3 | Reads the data with fixed column types | | `agent/mini_agent.R` | Shipped; first used here | The agent: three tools, its own permission rule and Manual-mode approvals | | `tests/test_translation.R` | Shipped; first used here | Compares a tidyverse translation with the original base R code | | `scripts/functions/summaries.R` | Written by your agent, with your approval, in Task 2 | The translation | | A line in `docs/ai-log.md` | You, in Task 2 | The record | **Before you start.** ellmer is the package that talks to Claude and runs the loop. It is pinned in your repository's `renv.lock`, so `renv::restore()` installed it. Never run `install.packages()` inside the project. Your key comes from an Anthropic Console account, which is separate from a Claude subscription. The key lives in your user-level `.Renviron`, outside every repository. Every request costs a little; Task 2 shows you how much the agent used. The page follows the order of Hadley Wickham's explainer [*What is an agent?*](https://substack.hadley.nz/p/what-is-an-agent): a conversation, then a tool, then the loop. Joseph Barbier's talk *50 lines of code to rebuild Claude Code in R* (R+AI 2026, scheduled for 10 November) shows how to build the same kind of agent; the version here is our own. ::: ## Task 1: a conversation, then a tool :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Talk to a model, then give it a tool (8 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **Goal:** see what one request to a model is, and what a tool request is, so that nothing your agent does in Task 2 is a surprise. **1. Have a conversation.** Run this in the R console: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} library(ellmer) key <- function() Sys.getenv("AGENT_ANTHROPIC_KEY") chat <- chat_anthropic(model = "claude-sonnet-5-5", credentials = key) chat$chat("Tell me a joke about R.") chat$chat("Explain why it is funny, in one sentence.") chat ``` ::: Printing `chat` shows the conversation as turnsOne message in a conversation with a model: either yours (the user turn) or the model’s reply (the assistant turn). Tool results go back to the model inside a user turn.. The second question works only because ellmer sends the **whole conversation so far** with each request: the model keeps nothing between requests. That is the [context window](11-AI-programming-integrated.qmd) from Block 1. It is also why a long conversation costs more per question. **2. Give it a tool.** A tool is an R function the model may ask you to run: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} today <- tool( function() format(Sys.Date()), name = "today", description = "Get today's date." ) chat <- chat_anthropic(model = "claude-sonnet-5-5", credentials = key) chat$register_tool(today) chat$chat("How many days until 25 December?") chat ``` ::: The model sees only the tool's name, description and arguments (here, none). Its first reply is a request: "call `today`". ellmer runs `today()` **on your computer** and sends the result back. Then the model answers. That is two requestsOne call to the model, with the whole conversation so far, and its reply. A single question can take several requests when the model asks for tools before it answers. for one question. **You are done when** you can point, in the printed `chat`, to the tool request and to the tool result, and say which of them ran on your computer. **If it goes wrong:** if the first `chat$chat()` reports a missing or invalid key, check `Sys.getenv("AGENT_ANTHROPIC_KEY") != ""`. Restart R after you edit `.Renviron`. :::: ::: ## The loop An agentAn assistant that can read across a project’s files and, depending on its permission mode, edit them and run commands, such as Claude Code. An agent acts; a chat window only advises. repeats that exchange until a reply asks for no tool. Each time, the harnessThe software around a model that keeps the conversation, sends it to the model, runs the tools the model asks for and sends back their results. Claude Code is a harness; so is a chat object made with ellmer. sends the conversation, runs any tool the model asks for, adds the result, and sends it all again. Every control in this course acts on one of three facts: - **The model only asks.** The harness runs each tool on your computer, so that is where Manual mode asks you, a deny rule refuses, and a hook inspects. - **Results go back to the model.** A tool that reads a data file sends that data to the provider: [Block 3's disclosure route](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd). - **The model decides when to stop.** It can loop longer than you expect. That is why a real harness has limits and a stop key. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## How it works: the loop with no model at all This code runs without an API key. It replaces the model with a pretend one that follows a script. Each pass of `repeat` is one request. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # the tools, as plain R functions tools <- list( n_rows = function(name) { nrow(get(name, envir = as.environment("package:datasets"))) } ) # a pretend model: asks for a tool until it has two results, then answers pretend_model <- function(turns) { results <- Filter(function(t) t$role == "tool result", turns) if (length(results) == 0) { list(role = "assistant", tool = "n_rows", args = list(name = "mtcars")) } else if (length(results) == 1) { list(role = "assistant", tool = "n_rows", args = list(name = "iris")) } else { list(role = "assistant", text = paste("iris has", results[[2]]$text, "rows and mtcars has", results[[1]]$text, "so iris has more.")) } } # the harness: send the conversation, run any tool asked for, repeat question <- "Which has more rows, mtcars or iris?" turns <- list(list(role = "user", text = question)) repeat { reply <- pretend_model(turns) turns <- c(turns, list(reply)) if (is.null(reply$tool)) break # no tool asked for: this is the answer result <- do.call(tools[[reply$tool]], reply$args) turns <- c(turns, list(list(role = "tool result", text = result))) } for (t in turns) { what <- if (is.null(t$tool)) t$text else paste0("call ", t$tool, "(", t$args, ")") cat(sprintf("%-12s %s\n", t$role, what)) } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` user Which has more rows, mtcars or iris? assistant call n_rows(mtcars) tool result 32 assistant call n_rows(iris) tool result 150 assistant iris has 150 rows and mtcars has 32 so iris has more. ``` ::: ::: `do.call()` is the only line that does anything to your computer: that is where Manual mode, deny rules and hooks act. In the real API the tool result goes back inside a user turn; ellmer does that for you. ::: ## Your agent: `agent/mini_agent.R` Your repository ships a complete agent of about 80 lines, built from the same parts. Your instructor walks through it. Each part matches something from this morning: - **Three tools.** `read_file()` looks around; `write_file()` changes a file; `run_test()` runs one test, `tests/test_translation.R`, in a fresh R session. - **`allowed()` is its deny rule.** The agent may read inside the project, but not credentials files. It may write **only under `scripts/`**, so it cannot edit its checks in `tests/` or its own rules in `agent/`. - **`ask_first()` is Manual mode.** Reads go straight through. Every write and every test run is shown to you first, and is refused unless you choose **Yes**. - **The system prompt is its instruction file.** The agent is not given your `AGENTS.md`, though it could still open the file, like any other. Like `AGENTS.md`, its prompt is only a request. Your agent can run one test and nothing else. A general run-R tool would let the model run any code. That is the gap Block 5 found: R code can write anywhere, whatever the deny rules say. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Reference: the full `agent/mini_agent.R` ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} # agent/mini_agent.R ---- # A small coding agent: Claude, three tools, and the loop ellmer runs for you. # Load it from your workshop repository with # source(here::here("agent", "mini_agent.R")) # then talk to `chat`. library(ellmer) # the model: "claude-opus-5-5" is a larger model, at a higher price per token model <- "claude-sonnet-5-5" # your API key, from the AGENT_ANTHROPIC_KEY line in your user-level .Renviron; # it has its own name so that Claude Code never offers to use it agent_key <- function() Sys.getenv("AGENT_ANTHROPIC_KEY") if (agent_key() == "") { stop("No AGENT_ANTHROPIC_KEY found: add it with usethis::edit_r_environ(), ", "then restart R.") } # the agent's deny rule: a path must sit inside `folder`, and never be a # credentials file ---- root <- here::here() allowed <- function(path, folder = root) { full <- fs::path_norm(fs::path_abs(path, start = root)) if (!fs::path_has_parent(full, folder) || fs::path_file(full) %in% c(".Renviron", ".env")) { stop("Refused: ", path) } full } # the tools ---- read_file <- tool( function(path) paste(readLines(allowed(path), warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n"), name = "read_file", description = "Read a text file in the project.", arguments = list(path = type_string("A file, relative to the project root.")) ) write_file <- tool( function(path, content) { writeLines(content, allowed(path, folder = fs::path(root, "scripts"))) paste("Wrote", path) }, name = "write_file", description = "Replace the whole contents of a text file under scripts/.", arguments = list( path = type_string("A file under scripts/, relative to the project root."), content = type_string("The complete new contents of the file.") ) ) run_test <- tool( function() { # the one thing it can run: the translation test, in a fresh R session out <- callr::r(function() utils::capture.output( testthat::test_file("tests/test_translation.R", reporter = "summary") )) paste(utils::tail(out, 40), collapse = "\n") }, name = "run_test", description = "Run tests/test_translation.R in a fresh R session and return its output." ) # Manual mode: show every write or test run, and ask before it happens ---- ask_first <- function(request) { if (request@name %in% c("write_file", "run_test")) { cat("\nThe agent wants to call", request@name, "with:\n") for (arg in names(request@arguments)) { cat("--", arg, "--\n", request@arguments[[arg]], "\n") } if (utils::menu(c("Yes", "No"), title = "Allow it?") != 1) tool_reject() } } chat <- chat_anthropic( model = model, credentials = agent_key, system_prompt = paste( "You are a careful R assistant working in this project.", "Read files before you change them. Write files only under scripts/;", "never edit tests/. Code you write must work in a fresh R session, so load", "packages with library() or call them with pkg::. Say what you changed,", "and stop when the task is done." ) ) chat$register_tools(list(read_file, write_file, run_test)) chat$on_tool_request(ask_first) ``` ::: An error in a tool does not stop the agent. ellmer sends the error message back to the model, which can try something else. So a refused write comes back as "Refused: …". `run_test()` uses a fresh R session (`callr::r()`), so it cannot change the objects in yours. Only the last 40 lines of its output go back to the model. ::: ## Task 2: run your agent :::{.task} ::::{.task-header} Run your agent (15 minutes) :::: ::::{.task-container} **Goal:** watch your own agent write, test and fix a translation while you approve every write and test run, so that you see exactly where Manual mode and a deny rule act. **Start state:** `main`, Git pane clean, R's working directory at the repository's root (as it is when you open the project). **1. Load the agent.** Nothing is sent to the model yet: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} source(here::here("agent", "mini_agent.R")) ``` ::: **2. Give it the task.** The original base R code is `legacy_rate_summary()` in `tests/test_translation.R`, which also checks the translation: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} chat$chat(paste( "Write a function summarise_rate_tidy(data) in scripts/functions/summaries.R", "whose output matches legacy_rate_summary() in tests/test_translation.R.", "Use dplyr and the native pipe; it must work in a fresh R session.", "Write only that file, and no tests. Then run the test with run_test,", "and fix the function until it passes." )) ``` ::: **3. Decide each request.** Reads run without asking. For a `write_file` request, read the code it prints. Choose **Yes** only for a write to `scripts/functions/summaries.R`. **Refuse the first `run_test` on purpose:** the agent usually stops and explains. If it asks again at once, answer No again. Then let it continue: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} chat$chat("Go ahead and run the test.") ``` ::: **4. Look inside.** ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} chat # every turn: your prompt, its tool requests, the results chat$get_tokens() # the tokens it sent and received ``` ::: **5. Check its work yourself.** When the agent says "the test passes", that is a claim. Read the diff of `scripts/functions/summaries.R` in the Git pane. Then restart R (*Session → Restart R*) and run: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} testthat::test_dir(here::here("tests")) ``` ::: `test_translation.R` is the test that matters here: it now passes rather than skips. The other files pass or skip, as before. **6. Record and commit.** Your agent can write only under `scripts/`, so it cannot draft this line as Claude Code did in Block 3: that is its write rule at work. Add the line to `docs/ai-log.md` yourself, with today's date, for example `2026-10-22; mini agent (ellmer, claude-sonnet-5-5); translated the rate summary to tidyverse; kept after reading the diff and running the tests`. Then commit `summaries.R` and the log.
`aggregate()` with a formula silently drops the animal whose `metabolic_rate_post` is missing, so the original's mean and count leave it out. A literal tidyverse translation keeps it: an `NA` mean and a count one too high. The test compares against the original, so the agent had to match that behaviour. If it read the test, it probably did so without comment. The test checks "the same as the original", not "correct": Block 8 returns to that difference.
**You are done when** `test_translation.R` passes in your own run, the Git pane showed only `summaries.R` and your log changed, you can say how many requests the task took (count the assistant turns in the printed `chat`) and how many tokens, and both are committed. **If it goes wrong:** - **The agent loops or goes off course:** answer **No**, then steer it with `chat$chat("…")`, or `source()` the file again to start a new conversation. - **A refused write:** the agent can write only under `scripts/`; read the path it asked for. - **`run_test` cannot find `tests/test_translation.R`:** check that `getwd()` is the repository's root. - **An unwanted change:** **Revert** it in the Git pane. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## What did it cost? `chat$get_cost()` turns the tokens into money when ellmer knows the model's price. If it shows `NA`, run `ellmer::models_update_prices()` once to refresh ellmer's price list. Or multiply the tokens from `chat$get_tokens()` by the prices on Anthropic's pricing page. `claude-opus-5-5`, named in the comment at the top of `mini_agent.R`, is a larger model at a higher price per token; to use it, change the `model` line. ::: :::: ::: ## What Claude Code adds | Your mini agent | Claude Code | |---|---| | `ask_first()` and `tool_reject()` | Manual mode (`default`) and the other permission modes | | `allowed()`: writes only under `scripts/` | Deny rules in `.claude/settings.json`, such as `Edit(/data/raw/**)` | | The system prompt | `AGENTS.md`, read at the start of each session | | `run_test()`, which can run one test and nothing else | Any command it asks to run, each with your approval | | `chat` and `chat$get_tokens()` | The conversation itself, and the model shown in Claude Code | | Git, to see and undo changes | Git, plus `/rewind`, which undoes only changes made with its edit tools ([Block 5](11f-enforced-controls.qmd)) | Claude Code adds plan mode, hooks, skills, compaction of long conversations, many more tools and far more checks around each one. You build the small version to understand the big one, not to use it for real work. In Block 7 you hand Claude Code a much bigger job under the same controls. :::{.callout-note} ## Check · Reproduce · Record - **You can now:** explain an agent as a model, a harness and tools in a loop, and run one in R, **trusted because** you can read every line that touches your files, and a test you did not write decides whether its change is right. - **Check:** every write and every run is shown to you before it happens; the Git pane shows what changed; the test runs in a fresh R session. - **Reproduce:** `run_test()` runs in a fresh R session, so the agent's check does not depend on what is loaded in yours. - **Record:** `chat` holds the full record of what was sent and received; your AI-use log records the tool, the model and what you kept. ::: ## Check your understanding **In an agent built with ellmer, who runs a tool's R function?**
**True or false: when an agent's tool reads a file, the file's contents are sent to the model provider.** **Your agent can write only under `scripts/`, and has no general run-R tool. What would adding one put at risk?**
## Going further (not covered live) This material is not covered in the live session. Work through it afterwards if it is useful to you. :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Add a general `run_r()` tool, and see the gap reopen Add this tool to `agent/mini_agent.R`. Paste it after `run_test`. Add `run_r` to the `register_tools()` list, and add `"run_r"` to the names that `ask_first()` asks about. Then `source()` the file again for a new conversation. (Redefining `ask_first()` in the console has no effect: the chat keeps the copy it was given.) ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code} run_r <- tool( function(code) { out <- callr::r(function(code) utils::capture.output( tryCatch(source(exprs = parse(text = code), print.eval = TRUE), error = function(e) cat("Error:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")) ), list(code = code)) paste(utils::head(out, 60), collapse = "\n") }, name = "run_r", description = "Run R code in a fresh R session; return its printed output.", arguments = list(code = type_string("The R code to run.")) ) ``` ::: Now the model can run any code: `writeLines()` into `data/raw/`, or `Sys.getenv()` for your key. `allowed()` no longer protects anything. Only your approval stands in the way, exactly as in Block 5. A narrow tool such as `run_test()` needs less trust than a general one. ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## A restricted mode Change `ask_first()` in `agent/mini_agent.R` so that it asks before every call, reads included. Then `source()` the file again. You now see every file the agent wants to read before it is sent to the provider. By default, Claude Code never asks before reading a project file ([Block 3](11d-context-disclosure-autonomy.qmd)). In your own agent, one line of R changes that, because you wrote its approval step. ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Packages that do more - [btw](https://posit-dev.github.io/btw/) gives ellmer agents ready-made tools for R: package documentation, your live session's objects and your project's files. - [mcptools](https://posit-dev.github.io/mcptools/) connects R to the Model Context Protocol, so R functions can be tools for other assistants, including Claude Code. ::: :::{.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Another provider ellmer has a `chat_*()` function for each provider it supports. The tools and the loop stay the same. Tool calling can be much less reliable with small local models, so start with a hosted model. ::: ## Glossary ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
term definition
agent An assistant that can read across a project's files and, depending on its permission mode, edit them and run commands, such as Claude Code. An agent acts; a chat window only advises.
harness The software around a model that keeps the conversation, sends it to the model, runs the tools the model asks for and sends back their results. Claude Code is a harness; so is a chat object made with ellmer.
request One call to the model, with the whole conversation so far, and its reply. A single question can take several requests when the model asks for tools before it answers.
turn One message in a conversation with a model: either yours (the user turn) or the model's reply (the assistant turn). Tool results go back to the model inside a user turn.
````` ::: ::: ## References - Wickham, H. (2026, 5 June). *What is an agent?* AI for data science (Substack). - Barbier, J.
